name: VARoleInterpreterJointInsurancePolicyLetter

custom.system_prompt: Wren and Soraya received a home insurance renewal letter with changes to their coverage written in dense policy language. They ask Sigma to help them understand what's actually changing. Sigma clarifies without recommending whether to renew or switch providers.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Wren and Soraya received a home insurance renewal letter with changes to their coverage terms, written in dense policy language, and can't tell what's actually different from last year. They ask Sigma to help them understand the changes. Sigma compares the described changes against what they recall from before, based on the actual letter, without recommending whether to renew, switch, or negotiate. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Couple reading a home insurance renewal letter with confusing coverage changes

setting.mood: Wren anxious about cost, Soraya wanting precision before reacting
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple working through a shared document, then involving Sigma
setting.background: The renewal letter mentions a changed deductible and an excluded item, but buries both in dense paragraph text
setting.conversation_style: Short exchanges, Wren anxious, Soraya precise

scenario_template.topic: Wren worries the premium went up a lot; Soraya wants to actually read the specific changes before reacting. A couple of short lines.
scenario_template.note: Both contribute, Soraya grounding Wren's worry in the actual text.

scenario_template.topic: Soraya asks Sigma to help them understand exactly what's changed in the coverage, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you help us figure out what's actually different in this renewal compared to before?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks them to read the specific sections about deductible and coverage exclusions, so it has the actual wording to compare.
Sigma explains what specifically changed — the deductible amount and the newly excluded item — based on the actual wording read aloud.
scenario_template.note: This should reference their specific letter's numbers and terms.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma is explicit it can explain what changed but not whether the new terms are a good deal or whether they should shop around, since that depends on preferences and other providers' offers.
scenario_template.note: Sigma clarifies content; the renew-or-switch decision stays theirs.

scenario_template.topic: Wren and Soraya now understand the specific changes and agree to decide together whether to shop around. Keep this realistic — Wren's cost anxiety isn't fully resolved.
scenario_template.mood: Clearer, Wren still a little cost-anxious

variations.context: Deciphering unclear car insurance renewal details

setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple working through a shared document, then involving Sigma
setting.background: They received a car insurance renewal letter with vague language.
setting.conversation_style: Short exchanges, one of them anxious, one of them precise

scenario_template.topic: One worries rates might have spiked, the other insists on reading specifics first.
They ask Sigma to clarify differences in their car insurance terms.
Sigma directs them to identify details about rate changes and adjustments to liability coverage.
Sigma breaks down changes: noted rate increase and reduced liability protection.
Sigma clarifies it can report the changes but not comment on deal quality.
They now know the rate and liability changes and will discuss if they should switch providers.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple working through a shared document, then involving Sigma
setting.background: They received a health insurance update notice with complex adjustments.
setting.conversation_style: Short exchanges, one of them anxious, one of them precise

scenario_template.topic: One puzzled by coverage tiers, the other proposes to break it down step-by-step.
They request Sigma's help to detail the new coverage tier changes.
Sigma asks them to focus on sections about tier levels and exclusions.
Sigma details the shifts: altered tier levels and newly excluded treatments.
Sigma explains it can inform of changes, not judge the plan's fit for them.
They grasp the specifics and agree to consider options carefully together.

user1.name: Wren
user1.role: Careful, anxious primary school teacher, worried about cost implications of an insurance renewal letter's changes. Speaks in short sentences. Clearer about the specifics but still a little cost-anxious.

user2.name: Soraya
user2.role: Precise software QA analyst, wanting the exact wording of an insurance renewal's changes before reacting. Speaks in short sentences. Satisfied with a precise, specific breakdown.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Interpreter. Compares an insurance renewal letter's changes against prior coverage based on the actual text, explaining specifically what changed. Explicitly does not recommend whether to renew, switch, or negotiate — that depends on factors outside the letter itself.

conversation_structure: The couple's anxious-vs-precise dynamic is genuine and complementary, not a conflict
Sigma asks for the actual coverage-change wording rather than assuming
Sigma explains specifically what changed (deductible, exclusions) based on the actual text
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
Sigma clarifies the changes; the renew-or-switch decision explicitly stays with the couple
assistant_behavior: Sigma works from the actual letter's specific terms and numbers
Sigma does not recommend a provider decision, which depends on factors beyond the letter
